Elon Musk Promises to Give Out SpaceX Shares to U.S. Children
 
Plus, Saudi Arabia postpones flagship investor conference and U.S. steelmaker projects record profits.
 
By Heard on the Street Staff
 
 
JULIA DEMAREE NIKHINSON/ASSOCIATED PRESS
 

This is an edition of the Markets P.M. newsletter, a recap of the day’s most important markets moves, delivered after the closing bell. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 
 
 

What Happened in Markets Today

 

Elon Musk said he would gift every American child a SpaceX share, after Anthropic and other billionaires pledged to give away some of their wealth. Based on the current stock price and the number of U.S. children under the age of 18, that would come out to roughly $10 billion in stock.

 

Saudi Arabia postponed its ‘Davos in the Desert’ event that was scheduled for next week, as Houthi attacks raised security concerns. Organizers told attendees that it would be held off until next year. Attendees had been consulting security teams about the risks, including concerns that hotels and landmarks around the conference could become targets.

 

Steelmaker Cleveland-Cliffs’ shares jumped 16% after the company said during its results that its 2027 profit will be the highest since 2021 because of tight supply.

 

Tech stocks rebounded, with the Nasdaq Composite rising 1.1%. The S&P 500 added 0.4%, while the Dow shed 0.1%, or 36 points.

One Big Story

 
 
RACHEL MENDELSON/WSJ; PHILIP MONTGOMERY FOR WSJ, MICHAEL NAGLE/BLOOMBERG NEWS
 

Hedge-fund billionaire John Overdeck is facing a divorce trial with his wife and a standoff with his co-founder at Two Sigma, an $85 billion quant-trading giant. His wife is seeking a cash payment equivalent to 35% of his stake in Two Sigma. Being forced to liquidate that much of his stake could tip the firm’s control into Siegel’s favor. Some investors have had enough of the co-founders’ feud and have pulled their money out.
